b1.texto:
There are two ways to say what your name is, and both are correct:

- **Me llamo Ana.**
- **Soy Ana.**

To ask: **¿Cómo te llamas?**

Spanish almost never needs the pronoun. «Soy» already says «I am», so «yo soy» is only used when you want to insist.
b4.texto:
The verb **ser** is used for a name, origin and nationality.

- yo **soy**
- tú **eres**
- él / ella / usted **es**

Notice that each form already says who is speaking, which is why the pronoun is almost never needed.
b5.f0.texto: In the classroom there is a big map with names that Minh doesn't know.
b5.f1.texto: The teacher opens it carefully and asks, one by one, where each student comes from.
b5.f2.texto: Minh says the name in a low voice when he reaches his country, as if he were using it for the first time.
b5.f3.texto: Carmen, beside him, smiles and repeats the word slowly so that it sounds right.
b5.f4.texto: At the end of the class, everyone writes their name on a small piece of paper and sticks it next to the map.
b5.f5.texto: Minh looks at the wall for a while and sees twenty names and twenty different places.
b5.f6.texto: «Encantado», he says to the person next to him, and he discovers that this word, which he learned this morning, is already good for something real.
b6.o1.refuerzo: A man says that. The ending changes.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Gracias» is for thanking someone, not for meeting them.
b6.pregunta: Ana, a woman, meets someone. What does she say?
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Es» goes with él, ella or usted.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «My name is Ana».
intro: Today you learn to say your name and where you're from, and to ask other people. You also meet the verb «ser».
p.España.consejo: The eñe sounds like the «ny» in «canyon».
p.Vietnam.consejo: In Spanish the v is pronounced like a soft b.
p.cómo.consejo: With an accent when it asks; without one in «como tú», which compares.
p.de dónde.consejo: It asks about origin. «dónde» takes an accent because it's a question.
p.encantada.consejo: A woman says it. Only the last letter changes.
p.encantado.consejo: A man says it. It comes from «encantar»: I'm very glad.
p.eres.consejo: It's «ser» with «tú». The first e is pronounced clearly.
p.me llamo.consejo: In many areas «ll» sounds like the y in «yes». Literally: «I call myself».
p.soy.consejo: A single syllable. It already means «yo soy», so you don't need to say «yo».
p.te llamas.consejo: It's the «tú» form: you say it to the other person.
p.tú.consejo: With an accent when it's the pronoun «tú».
p.y.consejo: It sounds like the letter i.
p.mapa.consejo: Stress the first syllable: «MA-pa». It looks like the English word «map» with an extra vowel.
p.nombres.consejo: Plural of «nombre». Since it ends in s, the stress falls on the second-to-last syllable: «NOM-bres».
p.conoce.consejo: From «conocer». The «c» before «o» sounds like «k», and before «e» it sounds like a soft «th».
p.estudiante.consejo: Its root is «estudiar», to study. The stress falls on the third syllable: «es-tu-DYAN-te».
p.país.consejo: The accent mark on «í» shows the stress on the last syllable: «pa-IS». It is a short, clear word.
p.voz.consejo: At the end of a word, z sounds like a soft «th» in Spain. Its plural is «voces», with c.
p.usara.consejo: From «usar». After «como si», Spanish uses this form ending in -ara: «como si lo usara».
p.primera.glosa: first (por primera vez: for the first time)
p.primera.consejo: From «primero». Use «primera» before feminine nouns, as in «primera vez» for «first time».
p.vez.glosa: time (por primera vez: for the first time)
p.vez.consejo: In Spain the z sounds like a soft «th». It is the root of «veces»: «una vez», «dos veces».
p.lado.consejo: It usually appears in «al lado de», meaning next to. Learn the three words together as one phrase.
p.sonríe.consejo: From «sonreír», related to «sonrisa», the smile. The accent on the «í» splits the last two vowels.
p.palabra.consejo: Stress falls on «LA». Between vowels the b is softer, almost like a «v».
p.ayudarlo.consejo: The verb «ayudar» with «lo» (him) attached at the end. Similar: «ayudarla» for her, «ayudarte» for you.
p.pronunciarla.consejo: The infinitive «pronunciar» plus «la», which agrees with «palabra». In Spain, c before i sounds like «th».
p.todos.consejo: Plural of «todo». Use «todos» for a mixed or all-male group, and «todas» for an all-female group.
p.escriben.consejo: From «escribir». The «c» before «r» sounds like «k», and the stress falls on «KRI» in «es-KRI-ben».
p.nombre.consejo: Stress falls on «NOM», the first syllable. Its plural «nombres» keeps the same stress pattern.
p.papel.consejo: The stress falls on the last syllable, «pa-PEL», and the final l is clear, as in English «hotel».
p.pegan.consejo: From «pegar». The g stays hard here, like in «gato». Think of «pegamento», glue, to remember it.
p.junto.consejo: «junto» means together. Here it means right beside, as in «junto al mapa»: next to the map.
p.pared.consejo: «pared» is feminine: «la pared». It ends in d, so the stress falls on the last syllable.
p.lugares.consejo: The singular is «lugar», masculine: «el lugar». In the plural add -es; the stress stays on «ga».
p.diferentes.consejo: Its singular is «diferente», the same for both genders. Adding an s makes the plural.
p.compañero.consejo: The «ñ» sounds like «ny». Think of «compañía», company: a «compañero» shares your time.
p.descubre.consejo: From «descubrir»: «des-» undoes «cubrir», to cover. To discover is to uncover what was hidden.
p.aprendida.consejo: Its ending -da agrees with «palabra», a feminine noun. Participles change their ending to match.
p.sirve.consejo: In Spanish «v» sounds like «b». So «sirve» is pronounced «SIR-be», with the stress on «SIR».
p.yo.consejo: Spanish often drops «yo» because the verb ending already says who speaks. Here it is kept for clarity.
p.pregunta.consejo: The stress falls on «GUN»: pre-GUN-ta. Here the «u» is pronounced, and «g» stays hard.
